chapters.title: A closed gate
paragraphs: Mara kept the harbor ledger. After a storm, the council closed the east gate because its hinges were cracked. No ship was lost in the storm.
Ilan wanted the gate reopened immediately to save the market. Mara asked for a hinge inspection before a vote.

chapters.title: The trial
paragraphs: The inspection found two cracked hinges. Repairing both would take three days. Mara proposed a temporary west landing, with a limit of two boats each hour.
The council accepted a one-day trial. The ledger records twelve deliveries and one damaged crate. It does not record the value of the crate.

chapters.title: An open ledger
paragraphs: Ilan changed his vote after reading the trial ledger. He said the count of deliveries mattered more to him than winning the argument.
Mara wrote that a public record can expose mistakes but cannot choose which risks a town should accept. The council repaired the east gate and kept a public ledger.

chapters.title: A dry week
paragraphs: Sena managed a shared orchard. During a dry week, she suspended watering at noon because the uncovered channel lost water in the heat. No tree died that week.
Tovan demanded equal watering hours for every plot. Sena asked him to compare soil moisture before deciding what equal treatment meant.

chapters.title: The shaded channel
paragraphs: Measurements showed the hillside plot was drier than the lower plot. Sena proposed covering the channel and testing an evening schedule for four days.
The test used eight buckets on the hillside and five below. Fruit was counted after the test, but no price or sales revenue was recorded.

chapters.title: Sharing a decision
paragraphs: Tovan supported the evening schedule after seeing the moisture records. He said identical hours had hidden different needs.
Sena wrote that measurements can reveal a difference but cannot decide what a community owes each grower. The group kept the cover and agreed to review water allocations weekly.
